```{r}
library(tidyverse)

```

# Problem 1
```{r function_plot}

birthday_sim = function(n) {
  any(duplicated(sample(1:365, n, replace = TRUE)))
}

set.seed(2026)

birthday_results =
  tibble(n = 2:50) |>
  mutate(
    prob = map_dbl(n, \(x) mean(replicate(10000, birthday_sim(x))))
  )

birthday_results |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = prob)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Group size",
    y = "Probability of shared birthday"
  )
```
The probability of sharing a birthday increases with group size. When group size is larger than 23, the probability of sharing a birthday reaches 50%.

# Problem 2
```{r import}
subject_files =
  tibble(file = list.files("data", pattern = "\\.csv$")) |>
  mutate(data = map(file, \(x) read_csv(file.path("data", x))))

study_data =
  subject_files |>
  unnest(data) |>
  mutate(
    subject_id = str_remove(file, "\\.csv$"),
    arm = if_else(str_detect(file, "^con"), "Control", "Experimental")
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    values_to = "outcome"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.integer(week)) |>
  select(subject_id, arm, week, outcome)
```

```{r spaghetti-plot}
study_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome, group = subject_id)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(~ arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome"
  )
```

In the control group, the outcome fluctuated around the mean over time, while in the experimental group the outcome increased over time.

# problem 3

```{r Generating_simulation}
sim_t_test = function(mu) {
  x = rnorm(30, mean = mu, sd = 5)
  t.test(x, mu = 0) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    select(estimate, p.value)
}

set.seed(2026)

simulation_results =
  expand_grid(mu = 0:6, sim = 1:5000) |>
  mutate(
    result = map(mu, sim_t_test)
  ) |>
  unnest(result) |>
  mutate(rejected = p.value < 0.05)

simulation_summary =
  simulation_results |>
  group_by(mu) |>
  summarize(
    power = mean(rejected),
    mean_estimate = mean(estimate),
    mean_rejected = mean(estimate[rejected])
  )
```

```{r plot}
simulation_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mu, y = power)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "True mean",
    y = "Power"
  )


simulation_summary |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(mean_estimate, mean_rejected),
    names_to = "type",
    values_to = "estimate"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mu, y = estimate, color = type)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "True mean",
    y = "Average estimate"
  )
```

Power increases as the true mean increases.

The average estimate across all tests is close to the true mean. Because the sample mean is an unbiased estimator.
